```{r figures, include=FALSE}
## Every plot of the deck is drawn here, in the colours of the template,
## and saved under intro-figures/ so that the slides only include files.
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"
dir.create("intro-figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

fig <- function(name, width, height, expr, mar = c(2.8, 3.0, 0.8, 0.5)) {
  pdf(file.path("intro-figures", name), width = width, height = height)
  par(mar = mar, mgp = c(1.7, 0.5, 0), tcl = -0.3, las = 1, bty = "l",
      cex.axis = 0.85, cex.lab = 0.95)
  force(expr)
  dev.off()
}

## components of a statistical model: 100 coin tosses
fig("binom100.pdf", 4.2, 3.2, {
  k <- 0:100
  plot(k, dbinom(k, 100, 0.5), pch = 16, cex = 0.45, col = crukdark,
       xlab = "Number of heads", ylab = "Probability", ylim = c(0, 0.1))
  legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression("Probability, " * italic(p) * " = 0.5"),
                    expression("Number of tosses, " * italic(N) * " = 100")))
})

## small icon used in the frequentist inference cycle
fig("mini-dist.pdf", 3.0, 2.0, mar = c(1.6, 1.6, 0.3, 0.3), {
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 40), ylim = c(0, 0.2), xlab = "", ylab = "",
       cex.axis = 0.6)
  points(0:20, dbinom(0:20, 20, 0.5), pch = 16, cex = 0.45, col = crukdark)
  points(0:20, dbinom(0:20, 20, 0.7), pch = 16, cex = 0.45, col = cruklight)
  points(0:40, dbinom(0:40, 40, 0.5), pch = 16, cex = 0.45, col = crukpink)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.55, pch = 16,
         col = c(crukdark, cruklight, crukpink),
         legend = c("p = 0.5, n = 20", "p = 0.7, n = 20", "p = 0.5, n = 40"))
})

## continuous data: histogram of weight (density scale, unequal classes)
fig("hist-weight.pdf", 3.6, 2.8, mar = c(2.8, 4.0, 0.8, 0.5), {
  par(mgp = c(2.8, 0.5, 0))
  br <- c(0, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 130); n <- c(10, 10, 23, 45, 40, 47)
  dens <- n / (sum(n) * diff(br))
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 130), ylim = c(0, 0.03), xlab = "",
       ylab = "Density", xaxt = "n")
  axis(1, at = br, mgp = c(1.7, 0.5, 0))
  mtext("Weight (kg)", side = 1, line = 1.7, cex = 0.95)
  rect(head(br, -1), 0, br[-1], dens, col = cruklight, border = "white")
})

## IQR: simulated data on a line, with Q1, median, Q3 and the IQR
fig("iqr.pdf", 6.4, 1.6, mar = c(0.1, 0.4, 0.1, 0.4), {
  set.seed(7)
  x <- sort(round(rnorm(21, mean = 80, sd = 12), 1))
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75))
  par(xpd = NA)
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(x) + c(-4, 4), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.3), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  segments(min(x) - 4, 0, max(x) + 4, 0, col = "grey55", lwd = 1.3)
  rect(q[1], -0.28, q[3], 0.28, col = adjustcolor(crukpink, 0.12), border = NA)
  points(x, rep(0, length(x)), pch = 21, bg = cruklight, col = crukdark, cex = 1.15)
  segments(q, -0.42, q, 0.42, col = c(crukpink, crukdark, crukpink), lwd = 2)
  text(q, -0.68, sprintf(c("Q1 = %.1f", "Median = %.1f", "Q3 = %.1f"), q),
       col = c(crukpink, crukdark, crukpink), cex = 0.78, font = 2)
  text(mean(range(x)), -1.12, "Q1, median and Q3 are the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the data",
       col = "grey35", cex = 0.68)
  arrows(q[1], 0.72, q[3], 0.72, code = 3, angle = 90, length = 0.04, col = crukpink, lwd = 2)
  text(mean(q[c(1, 3)]), 1.08, sprintf("IQR = Q3 - Q1 = %.1f - %.1f = %.1f", q[3], q[1], q[3] - q[1]),
       col = crukpink, cex = 0.8, font = 2)
})

## normal distributions
fig("normals.pdf", 3.8, 2.9, {
  xs <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 600)
  pars <- list(c(0, 0.2), c(0, 1), c(0, 5), c(-2, 0.5))
  cols <- c(crukdark, crukpink, "grey50", cruklight)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(-5, 5), ylim = c(0, 0.92), xlab = "x",
       ylab = expression(varphi[list(mu, sigma^2)](x)))
  for (i in 1:4) lines(xs, dnorm(xs, pars[[i]][1], sqrt(pars[[i]][2])), col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = cols, cex = 0.75,
         legend = c(expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma^2 == 0.2), expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma^2 == 1),
                    expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma^2 == 5), expression(mu == -2 * "," ~ sigma^2 == 0.5)))
})

## other distributions: five small panels
fig("other-dists.pdf", 6.6, 4.1, mar = c(3.0, 2.8, 1.4, 0.4), {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3))
  cols <- c(crukdark, cruklight, crukpink)
  ttl <- function(s) title(s, font.main = 2, cex.main = 1.05, line = 0.4)
  ## hypergeometric
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 60), ylim = c(0, 0.15), xlab = "k", ylab = "PMF")
  K <- c(50, 60, 70); nn <- c(100, 200, 300)
  for (i in 1:3) { k <- 0:60; points(k, dhyper(k, K[i], 500 - K[i], nn[i]), pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = cols[i]) }
  legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, pch = 16, col = cols,
         legend = c("N=500, K=50, n=100", "N=500, K=60, n=200", "N=500, K=70, n=300"))
  ttl("Hypergeometric")
  ## beta
  xs <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 400)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 4.2), xlab = "x", ylab = "PDF")
  ab <- list(c(0.5, 0.5), c(2, 2), c(2, 5), c(5, 1))
  bc <- c(crukdark, cruklight, crukpink, "grey50")
  for (i in 1:4) lines(xs, dbeta(xs, ab[[i]][1], ab[[i]][2]), col = bc[i], lwd = 1.8)
  legend("top", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, lwd = 1.8, col = bc, ncol = 2,
         legend = c("a=0.5, b=0.5", "a=2, b=2", "a=2, b=5", "a=5, b=1"))
  ttl("Beta")
  ## gamma
  xs <- seq(0, 20, length.out = 400)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 20), ylim = c(0, 0.5), xlab = "x", ylab = "PDF")
  ks <- list(c(1, 2), c(2, 2), c(3, 2), c(9, 0.5)); gc <- c(crukdark, cruklight, crukpink, "grey50")
  for (i in 1:4) lines(xs, dgamma(xs, shape = ks[[i]][1], scale = ks[[i]][2]), col = gc[i], lwd = 1.8)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, lwd = 1.8, col = gc,
         legend = c(expression(k == 1 * "," ~ theta == 2), expression(k == 2 * "," ~ theta == 2),
                    expression(k == 3 * "," ~ theta == 2), expression(k == 9 * "," ~ theta == 0.5)))
  ttl("Gamma")
  ## log-normal
  xs <- seq(0.001, 3, length.out = 400)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.8), xlab = "x", ylab = "PDF")
  sg <- c(1, 0.25, 0.5)
  for (i in 1:3) lines(xs, dlnorm(xs, 0, sg[i]), col = cols[i], lwd = 1.8)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, lwd = 1.8, col = cols,
         legend = c(expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 1), expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 0.25),
                    expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 0.5)))
  ttl("Log\u00adnormal")
  ## Weibull
  xs <- seq(0.001, 2.5, length.out = 400)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 2.5), ylim = c(0, 2.5), xlab = "x", ylab = "PDF")
  ws <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 5); wc <- c(crukdark, cruklight, crukpink, "grey50")
  for (i in 1:4) lines(xs, dweibull(xs, ws[i], 1), col = wc[i], lwd = 1.8)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", cex = 0.7, lwd = 1.8, col = wc,
         legend = c(expression(lambda == 1 * "," ~ k == 0.5), expression(lambda == 1 * "," ~ k == 1),
                    expression(lambda == 1 * "," ~ k == 1.5), expression(lambda == 1 * "," ~ k == 5)))
  ttl("Weibull")
})

## confidence intervals: 20 samples of size 10 from N(0, 1)
fig("ci-sim.pdf", 3.0, 3.4, mar = c(2.6, 2.2, 0.6, 0.4), {
  set.seed(1)
  m <- 20; n <- 10
  ci <- t(replicate(m, { x <- rnorm(n); mean(x) + c(0, -1, 1) * qt(0.975, n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n) }))
  miss <- ci[, 2] > 0 | ci[, 3] < 0
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1.8, 1.8), ylim = c(m + 0.5, 0.5), xlab = "Sample estimate",
       ylab = "", yaxt = "n")
  axis(2, at = 1:m, labels = 1:m, cex.axis = 0.55)
  abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  segments(ci[, 2], 1:m, ci[, 3], 1:m, lwd = 2, col = ifelse(miss, crukpink, crukdark))
  points(ci[, 1], 1:m, pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = ifelse(miss, crukpink, crukdark))
  mtext(expression(theta), side = 3, at = 0, line = -0.2, cex = 0.9)
})

## central limit theorem: exact sampling distribution of the mean for four populations
## (no simulation noise: for a normal population the mean is exactly N(0, 1/n) for every n)
fig("clt-sim.pdf", 6.4, 4.4, mar = c(0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4), {
  ua <- 1.7
  dmean_unif <- function(x, n, h = 0.002) {        # n-fold convolution of U(-ua, ua), midpoint grid
    g <- seq(-ua + h / 2, ua - h / 2, by = h); f <- rep(1 / (2 * ua), length(g)); s <- f
    for (i in seq_len(n - 1)) s <- convolve(s, rev(f), type = "open") * h
    sg <- -n * ua + n * h / 2 + (seq_along(s) - 1) * h
    n * approx(sg, s, xout = n * x, yleft = 0, yright = 0)$y
  }
  pops <- list(
    Normal  = list(d = function(x) dnorm(x),                  dm = function(x, n) dnorm(x, 0, 1 / sqrt(n)),                xl = c(-3.5, 3.5)),
    Uniform = list(d = function(x) dunif(x, -ua, ua),         dm = dmean_unif,                                             xl = c(-2.2, 2.2)),
    Skewed  = list(d = function(x) dexp(x + 1),               dm = function(x, n) n * dgamma(n * (x + 1), shape = n, rate = 1), xl = c(-1.2, 4)),
    Bimodal = list(d = function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -1.5, 0.5) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 1.5, 0.5),
                   dm = function(x, n) { k <- 0:n; w <- dbinom(k, n, 0.5)
                     rowSums(sapply(seq_along(k), function(i) w[i] * dnorm(x, 1.5 * (2 * k[i] - n) / n, 0.5 / sqrt(n)))) },
                   xl = c(-3.5, 3.5)))
  ns <- c(2, 10, 30)
  par(mfrow = c(4, 4), oma = c(0.2, 6.0, 1.6, 0.2))
  for (row in 0:3) for (j in seq_along(pops)) {
    p <- pops[[j]]
    x <- seq(p$xl[1], p$xl[2], length.out = 2000)
    y <- if (row == 0) p$d(x) else p$dm(x, ns[row])
    plot(NULL, xlim = p$xl, ylim = c(0, max(y) * 1.08), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
    polygon(c(x, rev(x)), c(y, rep(0, length(x))), col = if (row == 0) "grey85" else adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.35), border = NA)
    lines(x, y, col = if (row == 0) "grey40" else crukdark, lwd = 1.4)
    abline(h = 0, col = "grey60")
    if (row > 0) segments(0, 0, 0, approx(x, y, xout = 0)$y, col = crukpink, lty = 2)
    box(col = "grey80")
    if (row == 0) mtext(names(pops)[j], side = 3, line = 0.4, cex = 0.8, font = 2)
    if (j == 1) mtext(c("Population", "n = 2", "n = 10", "n = 30")[row + 1], side = 2, line = 0.6, las = 1, adj = 1, cex = 0.75, font = 2)
  }
})

## Student's t distribution family
fig("tdist.pdf", 3.8, 2.9, {
  xs <- seq(-4.5, 4.5, length.out = 600)
  nus <- c(1, 2, 5, Inf); cols <- c("grey55", crukpink, cruklight, crukdark)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(-4.5, 4.5), ylim = c(0, 0.41), xlab = "t", ylab = "Probability density")
  for (i in 1:4) lines(xs, dt(xs, nus[i]), col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = cols, cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression(nu == 1), expression(nu == 2), expression(nu == 5),
                    expression(nu == +infinity)))
})

## p-value: sampling distribution of the test statistic under H0
fig("pvalue.pdf", 4.0, 2.6, mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), {
  xs <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 600)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(-4, 4), ylim = c(0, 0.46), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  tt <- seq(-4, -2.5, length.out = 100)
  polygon(c(tt, rev(tt)), c(dnorm(tt), rep(0, 100)), col = crukpink, border = NA)
  lines(xs, dnorm(xs), col = crukdark, lwd = 2)
  axis(1, at = c(-4, -2.5, 0, 2, 4), cex.axis = 0.8)
  segments(0, 0, 0, dnorm(0), lty = 2, col = "grey40")
  arrows(-2.7, 0.15, -2.85, 0.02, length = 0.07, col = crukpink, lwd = 1.5)
  text(-2.4, 0.19, "p\u00advalue = 0.0062", col = crukpink, cex = 0.75, font = 2)
  text(-2.5, -0.035, expression(t[s]), xpd = NA, cex = 0.9, col = crukdark, pos = 1, offset = 1.1)
  mtext("Test statistic (z-score)", side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 0.8)
})

## sign test: family of Bin(n, 0.5), in the style of the t-distribution family
fig("binomfam.pdf", 3.8, 2.9, mar = c(2.8, 3.8, 0.8, 0.5), {
  ns <- c(5, 10, 20); cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, crukdark)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 20), ylim = c(0, 0.33), xlab = "s", ylab = "")
  title(ylab = "P(S = s)", line = 2.5)
  for (i in 1:3) { k <- 0:ns[i]; lines(k, dbinom(k, ns[i], 0.5), col = cols[i], lwd = 1.2)
                   points(k, dbinom(k, ns[i], 0.5), pch = 16, cex = 0.7, col = cols[i]) }
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = cols, cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression(italic(n) == 5), expression(italic(n) == 10), expression(italic(n) == 20)))
})

## Wilcoxon signed-rank test: family of null distributions of W+
fig("signrankfam.pdf", 3.8, 2.9, mar = c(2.8, 3.8, 0.8, 0.5), {
  ns <- c(5, 8, 12); cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, crukdark)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 78), ylim = c(0, 0.1), xlab = expression(italic(w)), ylab = "")
  title(ylab = expression(P(italic(W)^"+" == italic(w))), line = 2.5)
  for (i in 1:3) { w <- 0:(ns[i] * (ns[i] + 1) / 2); lines(w, dsignrank(w, ns[i]), col = cols[i], lwd = 1.2)
                   points(w, dsignrank(w, ns[i]), pch = 16, cex = 0.55, col = cols[i]) }
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = cols, cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression(italic(n) == 5), expression(italic(n) == 8), expression(italic(n) == 12)))
})

## Wilcoxon rank-sum test: null distributions of W (sum of the ranks of sample 1)
fig("ranksumfam.pdf", 3.8, 2.9, mar = c(2.8, 3.8, 0.8, 0.5), {
  ns <- c(3, 5, 8); cols <- c(crukpink, cruklight, crukdark)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 0.16), xlab = expression(italic(w)), ylab = "")
  title(ylab = expression(P(italic(W) == italic(w))), line = 2.5)
  for (i in 1:3) { n <- ns[i]; u <- 0:(n * n); w <- u + n * (n + 1) / 2
                   lines(w, dwilcox(u, n, n), col = cols[i], lwd = 1.2)
                   points(w, dwilcox(u, n, n), pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = cols[i]) }
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, pch = 16, col = cols, cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression(italic(n)[1] == italic(n)[2] * " = 3"), expression(italic(n)[1] == italic(n)[2] * " = 5"),
                    expression(italic(n)[1] == italic(n)[2] * " = 8")))
})

## sign test: Bin(10, 0.5)
fig("binom10.pdf", 3.8, 2.4, {
  barplot(dbinom(0:10, 10, 0.5), names.arg = 0:10, col = cruklight, border = NA,
          ylab = "P(x)", xlab = "Number of successes (x)", ylim = c(0, 0.3))
})

## log-normal distribution, used for the transformation slides
fig("lognormal.pdf", 3.0, 2.8, {
  xs <- seq(0.001, 3, length.out = 400)
  sg <- c(1, 0.25, 0.5); cols <- c(crukdark, crukpink, cruklight)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 3), ylim = c(0, 1.75), xlab = "x", ylab = "PDF")
  for (i in 1:3) lines(xs, dlnorm(xs, 0, sg[i]), col = cols[i], lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = cols, cex = 0.8,
         legend = c(expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 1), expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 0.25),
                    expression(mu == 0 * "," ~ sigma == 0.5)))
})
```

## Roadmap

```{r process-flow, fig.width=6.6, fig.height=3.15, fig.align="center"}
crukdark <- "#00007E"

## everything the roadmap needs lives in its own environment, so later
## chunks that reuse names such as r or cx cannot change the drawing
draw_roadmap <- local({
  circle <- function(cx, cy, r, n = 200) {
    th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n)
    list(x = cx + r * cos(th), y = cy + r * sin(th))
  }


  stages <- c("Stage 1", "Stage 2", "Stage 3", "Stage 4", "Stage 5", "Stage 6")
  capt   <- list(c("Descriptive", "Statistics", ""),
                 c("Inferential", "Statistics", ""),
                 c("Normal", "Distribution", ""),
                 c("Testing", "Hypotheses", ""),
                 c("One-Sample", "Tests", ""),
                 c("Two-Sample", "Tests", ""))
  prefix <- c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)
  fills  <- c("#FF0087", "#009CEE", "#00007E", "#FF0087", "#009CEE", "#00007E")
  cx     <- c(1, 2.7, 4.4, 6.1, 7.8, 9.5)
  r      <- 0.64

  draw_line <- function(x, y, txt, cex, bold_prefix = NA,
                        col = "grey15", col_prefix = "black") {
    if (is.na(bold_prefix) || identical(txt, "")) {
      text(x, y, txt, cex = cex, col = col)
      return(invisible())
    }
    rest  <- sub(paste0("^", bold_prefix), "", txt)
    w1    <- strwidth(bold_prefix, cex = cex, font = 2)
    w2    <- strwidth(rest, cex = cex, font = 1)
    x0    <- x - (w1 + w2) / 2
    text(x0, y, bold_prefix, cex = cex, col = col_prefix, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0.5))
    text(x0 + w1, y, rest, cex = cex, col = col, adj = c(0, 0.5))
  }

  ## highlight = NA draws every stage in colour; a stage number greys out the others
  function(highlight = NA) {
    par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
    plot(NULL, xlim = c(0.28, 10.22), ylim = c(-1.85, 0.9), asp = 1,
         axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

    for (i in seq_along(cx)) {
      on  <- is.na(highlight) || i == highlight
      col <- if (on) "grey15" else "grey72"
      if (i < length(cx)) {
        arrows(cx[i] + r + 0.06, 0, cx[i + 1] - r - 0.06, 0,
               length = 0.13, lwd = 2.4, col = "grey55")
      }
      polygon(circle(cx[i], 0, r), col = if (on) fills[i] else "grey85", border = NA)
      text(cx[i], 0, stages[i], col = "white", cex = 1.12, font = 2)
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.24), capt[[i]][[1]], cex = 0.86, bold_prefix = prefix[i],
                col = col, col_prefix = if (on) "black" else "grey72")
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.50), capt[[i]][[2]], cex = 0.86, col = col)
      draw_line(cx[i], -(r + 0.76), capt[[i]][[3]], cex = 0.86, col = col)
    }
  }
})

draw_roadmap()
```

## Descriptive Statistics: Not the End Goal {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.1em-2.1pt\relax}

\noindent{\large What descriptive statistics \textbf{cannot} tell us: two questions.}\par

\newlength{\bulw}\settowidth{\bulw}{\bul\ }

\vspace{0.45em}

\noindent\bul\ \textcolor{crukdark}{\textbf{Generalisation / prediction}}\par

\vspace{-5.5pt}

```{=latex}
\noindent\hspace*{\bulw}\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.north)]
\node[inner sep=0, anchor=north west] (sam) at (0,0) {\includegraphics[height=1.25cm]{Sample.jpg}};
\node[inner sep=0, anchor=north west] (pop) at (3.45,0) {\includegraphics[height=1.25cm]{intro-figures/pop-crowd.jpg}};
\draw[-{Stealth[length=3mm]}, line width=1.3pt, crukpink] (sam.east) -- (pop.west);
\node[anchor=south, inner sep=0, font=\Large\bfseries, text=crukdark] at ($(sam.east)!0.5!(pop.west)+(0,0.12)$) {?};
\node[below=1pt of sam, font=\scriptsize, text=crukdark] {sample};
\node[below=1pt of pop, font=\scriptsize, text=crukdark] {population};
\node[anchor=west, text width=4.1cm, font=\small, align=left, execute at begin node={\hyphenpenalty=10000}] at (5.75,-0.62) {Do the results hold for \textbf{other} patients, mice or cells?};
\end{tikzpicture}\par
```

\vspace{\dimexpr0.8em+8.3pt\relax}

\noindent\bul\ \textcolor{crukdark}{\textbf{The signal-to-noise ratio problem}}\par

\vspace{-5.5pt}

```{=latex}
\noindent\hspace*{\bulw}\begin{tikzpicture}[baseline=(current bounding box.north)]
\foreach \x/\c/\lab in {0/cruklight/Cisplatin, 2.55/crukpink/Gefitinib} {
  \foreach \i in {0,...,3} {
    \fill[\c] (\x+0.155+\i*0.46, -0.13) circle (0.128);
    \fill[\c, rounded corners=1.4pt] (\x+\i*0.46, -0.78) rectangle (\x+0.31+\i*0.46, -0.30);
  }
  \draw[-{Stealth[length=2.6mm]}, line width=1.2pt, crukdark] (\x+0.845,-0.92) -- (\x+0.845,-1.46);
  \node[font=\scriptsize\bfseries, text=crukdark, anchor=north] at (\x+0.845,-1.50) {\lab};
}
\node[anchor=west, text width=4.6cm, font=\small, align=left, execute at begin node={\hyphenpenalty=10000}] at (5.75,-0.62) {Is the \textbf{difference} between the two treatments real, or just noise?};
\end{tikzpicture}\par
```

## Statistics ends with a superstructure built on data {.t}

\vspace{-1.0em}

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  lbl/.style={font=\normalsize\bfseries, text=crukdark},
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=3mm]}, line width=1.3pt, draw=crukpink},

% the black box

\node[txt, text width=7.55cm, anchor=north west, inner ysep=0pt] at (pop.north -| -2.2,0) {A \textbf{population} is the complete set of \textcolor{crukdark}{\textbf{real}} individuals (or objects, events, or measurements) about which we want to draw conclusions. hfig2 <- function(file, expr) {

```{r height-figures, include=FALSE}
}
hfig <- function(file, expr) {
  pdf(file, width = 3.6, height = 2.2)
  par(mar = c(2.6, 3.2, 1.3, 0.5), mgp = c(1.6, 0.45, 0), tcl = -0.3, las = 1, bty = "l",
      cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.85, cex.main = 0.95, font.main = 1)
  force(expr); dev.off()
}
## population: a normal model for adult height (mean 169 cm, SD 10 cm)
hfig("intro-figures/height-distribution.pdf", {
  x <- seq(140, 200, length.out = 400); y <- dnorm(x, 169, 10)
  par(mar = c(2.6, 3.9, 1.3, 0.5))
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(140, 200), ylim = c(0, 0.045), xlab = "Height (cm)",

  axis(2, at = seq(0, 0.04, 0.01))

  lines(x, y, col = cruklight, lwd = 2.5)
})
```

```{r height-parameters, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"
## the height distribution again, plain / with the mean / with mean and spread (mean 169 cm, SD 10 cm)
pfig <- function(file, mean_line = FALSE, spread = FALSE) {
  pdf(file, width = 3.6, height = 2.7)
  par(mar = c(3.1, 4.4, 1.5, 0.5), mgp = c(1.9, 0.5, 0), tcl = -0.3, las = 1, bty = "l",
      cex.axis = 0.95, cex.lab = 1.05, cex.main = 1.1, font.main = 1)
  x <- seq(140, 200, length.out = 400); y <- dnorm(x, 169, 10)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(140, 200), ylim = c(0, 0.045), xlab = "Height (cm)", ylab = "",
       main = "Height distribution", yaxt = "n")
  axis(2, at = seq(0, 0.04, 0.01)); title(ylab = "Probability density", line = 3.2)
  polygon(c(x, rev(x)), c(y, rep(0, length(x))), col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(x, y, col = cruklight, lwd = 2.5)
  if (mean_line) segments(169, 0, 169, 0.0435, lty = 2, lwd = 1.4, col = crukdark)
  if (spread) arrows(159, dnorm(159, 169, 10), 179, dnorm(179, 169, 10), code = 3,
                     length = 0.08, angle = 25, lwd = 1.4, col = crukdark)
  dev.off()
}
pfig("intro-figures/height-plain.pdf")
pfig("intro-figures/height-mean.pdf", mean_line = TRUE)
pfig("intro-figures/height-spread.pdf", mean_line = TRUE, spread = TRUE)
```

## Normal distribution {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em-2.5pt\relax}

\small A \textbf{normal distribution} or \textbf{Gaussian distribution} is a type of continuous probability distribution. It is determined by two parameters ($\mu$, $\sigma^2$).\normalsize

\vspace{1.4em}

\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\useasboundingbox (0,0.1) rectangle (10.9,-4.0);
\node[inner sep=0, anchor=north west] at (0,0) {\includegraphics[width=4.9cm]{intro-figures/height-spread.pdf}};

\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

```{r mc-population-model, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"

pdf("intro-figures/population-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 3
xlim  <- c(0, 15)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dchisq(xs, dfree)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.18),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)
axis(1, at = seq(0, 15, 3), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
dev.off()
```

```{r mc-population-bp, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"

pdf("intro-figures/population-bp.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

mu <- 110; sdev <- 15
xlim <- c(mu - 3.4 * sdev, mu + 3.4 * sdev)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dnorm(xs, mu, sdev)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.28),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

## mu: dashed vertical line through the peak
segments(mu, 0, mu, dnorm(mu, mu, sdev), col = crukdark, lty = 2, lwd = 1.6)
text(mu, dnorm(mu, mu, sdev), expression(mu), pos = 3, offset = 0.3,
     col = crukdark, cex = 2.2)

## sigma: from mu to mu + sigma, at the height of the inflection point
y_s <- dnorm(mu + sdev, mu, sdev)
arrows(mu, y_s, mu + sdev, y_s, code = 3, length = 0.08, angle = 25,
       col = crukdark, lwd = 1.8)
text(mu + sdev / 2, y_s, expression(sigma), pos = 3, offset = 0.3,
     col = crukdark, cex = 2.1)

axis(1, at = seq(70, 150, 20), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext("Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)", side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 0.92)
dev.off()
```

```{r mc-chisq-generic, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("intro-figures/chisq-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(3.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 9
ccrit <- qchisq(0.95, dfree)   # 16.92
cobs  <- 19.5                  # a generic observed statistic, p = 0.021
xlim  <- c(0, 30)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dchisq(xs, dfree)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, max(ys) * 1.18),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the 5% rejection region in the upper tail
xr <- seq(ccrit, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
polygon(c(xr, rev(xr)), c(dchisq(xr, dfree), rep(0, length(xr))),
        col = crukpink, border = NA)

## the p-value: the area beyond the observed statistic, hatched over the
## critical region so that it is visibly a SUBSET of the 5% (p = 0.021 < 0.05)
xp <- seq(cobs, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
polygon(c(xp, rev(xp)), c(dchisq(xp, dfree), rep(0, length(xp))),
        col = cruklight, border = NA, density = 32, angle = 45, lwd = 1.6)
segments(cobs, 0, cobs, dchisq(cobs, dfree), col = cruklight, lwd = 1.3)

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

axis(1, at = seq(0, 30, 5), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(chi^2), side = 1, line = 2.05, cex = 1.2)

segments(ccrit, 0, ccrit, dchisq(ccrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
text(ccrit - 0.3, 0.034, "5%", col = crukpink,
     cex = 0.96, adj = c(1, 0.5))

## pink "Critical region" box, sized to its text
lab <- "Critical region"
lcex <- 0.98
bx <- 17.5; by <- max(ys) * 0.78
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.22
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
arrows(bx - bw/2 * 0.35, by - bh, ccrit + 0.8, 0.008, length = 0.05,
       lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)

## light-blue "p-value" box, pointing at the area beyond t_s
lab <- expression(bolditalic(p) * bold("\u00advalue"))
bx <- 25.5; by <- max(ys) * 0.42
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.35
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = cruklight, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = cruklight, cex = lcex, font = 2)
arrows(bx - bw/2 * 0.3, by - bh, cobs + 1.6, 0.003, length = 0.05,
       lwd = 1.2, col = cruklight)

## the observed statistic, sitting on the axis
points(cobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.9)
text(cobs, 0.013, expression(italic(t)[s]), col = cruklight,
     cex = 1.14, font = 2, adj = c(0.5, 0))

text(15, max(ys) * 1.13,
     expression(chi^2 ~ "distribution," ~ df == 9),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.03)
dev.off()
```

```{r mc-tdist-onesample, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("intro-figures/t-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

dfree <- 5
tcrit <- qt(0.975, dfree)
tobs  <- 9.185387
## symmetric window, so that BOTH tails of the two-sided test are visible
xlim  <- c(-8.8, 8.8)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dt(xs, dfree)
ymax <- max(ys)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, ymax * 1.46),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the two 2.5% rejection regions
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  xx <- if (sgn < 0) seq(xlim[1], -tcrit, length.out = 400) else seq(tcrit, xlim[2], length.out = 400)
  polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(dt(xx, dfree), rep(0, length(xx))),
          col = crukpink, border = NA)
}

## the two-sided p-value: both areas beyond |t_s|, hatched on top of the
## critical region so that it is visibly a SUBSET of the 5%
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  xx <- if (sgn < 0) seq(xlim[1], -tobs, length.out = 300) else seq(tobs, xlim[2], length.out = 300)
  polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(dt(xx, dfree), rep(0, length(xx))),
          col = cruklight, border = cruklight, density = 40, angle = 45, lwd = 1.5)
}

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

axis(1, at = seq(-8, 8, 4), cex.axis = 1.02, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(italic(t)), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 1.2)

segments(-tcrit, 0, -tcrit, dt(-tcrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
segments( tcrit, 0,  tcrit, dt( tcrit, dfree), col = crukpink, lwd = 1.4)
text(-(tcrit + 0.30), 0.072, "2.5%", col = crukpink, cex = 0.94, adj = c(0.5, 0))
text( (tcrit + 0.30), 0.072, "2.5%", col = crukpink, cex = 0.94, adj = c(0.5, 0))

## pink "Critical region" boxes, one over each tail
lab  <- "Critical region"
lcex <- 0.90
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.18
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.5
for (sgn in c(-1, 1)) {
  bx <- sgn * 6.3; by <- ymax * 0.52
  rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
       border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
  text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
  arrows(bx - sgn * bw/2 * 0.75, by - bh, sgn * (tcrit + 1.0), 0.012,
         length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)
}

## the observed statistic, sitting on the axis
points(tobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.7)
text(tobs - 0.3, 0.030, expression(italic(t[s]) == 9.19), col = cruklight,
     cex = 1.0, font = 2, adj = c(1, 0))

## light-blue "p-value" box, with an arrow to each hatched tail
lab1 <- expression(bold("Two\u00adsided ") * bolditalic(p) * bold("\u00advalue"))
lab2 <- expression(bold("= 0.0003"))
bx <- 0; by <- ymax * 1.12
gap <- strheight("X", cex = lcex) * 1.35
bw2 <- strwidth(lab1, cex = lcex) * 1.12
bh2 <- strheight("X", cex = lcex) * 1.75
rect(bx - bw2/2, by - bh2, bx + bw2/2, by + bh2,
     border = cruklight, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by + gap/2, lab1, col = cruklight, cex = lcex)
text(bx, by - gap/2, lab2, col = cruklight, cex = lcex)
for (sgn in c(-1, 1))
  arrows(sgn * bw2/2, by - bh2 * 0.55, sgn * 8.0, 0.009,
         length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = cruklight)

text(0, ymax * 1.40, expression(italic(t) ~ "distribution," ~ df == 5),
     col = crukdark, cex = 1.0)
dev.off()
```

```{r est-generic, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("intro-figures/estimator-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(3.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

theta <- 0; se <- 1
tobs  <- 1.15
xlim  <- c(-3.6, 3.6)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dnorm(xs, theta, se)
ymax <- max(ys)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, ymax * 1.30),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

## the estimand: a dashed line at the true value
segments(theta, 0, theta, dnorm(theta, theta, se), col = crukpink, lty = 2, lwd = 1.6)
text(theta, dnorm(theta, theta, se), expression(theta), pos = 3, offset = 0.25,
     col = crukpink, cex = 1.5)

## the standard error, from theta to theta + se
y_s <- dnorm(theta + se, theta, se)
arrows(theta, y_s, theta + se, y_s, code = 3, length = 0.07, angle = 25,
       col = crukdark, lwd = 1.6)
text(theta + se / 2, y_s, "SE", pos = 3, offset = 0.25,
     col = crukdark, cex = 0.92, font = 2)

axis(1, at = seq(-3, 3, 1), labels = FALSE, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(hat(theta)), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 1.2)

## the observed estimate, sitting on the axis
points(tobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.8)
text(tobs + 0.12, 0.028, expression(bolditalic(hat(theta))), col = cruklight,
     cex = 1.15, adj = c(0, 0))

text(0, ymax * 1.25, "Sampling distribution of the estimator",
     col = crukdark, cex = 0.96)
dev.off()
```

```{r est-xbar, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("intro-figures/xbar-distribution.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 3.0)
par(mar = c(2.6, 0.5, 0.9, 0.5), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

xbar <- 133.17; se <- 2.52
tcrit <- qt(0.975, 5)
lo <- xbar - tcrit * se; hi <- xbar + tcrit * se
xlim <- c(xbar - 3.6 * se, xbar + 3.6 * se)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 1200)
ys <- dnorm(xs, xbar, se)
ymax <- max(ys)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, ymax * 1.46),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## the central 95% of the sampling distribution
xx <- seq(lo, hi, length.out = 600)
polygon(c(xx, rev(xx)), c(dnorm(xx, xbar, se), rep(0, length(xx))),
        col = cruklight, border = NA, density = 34, angle = 45, lwd = 1.5)

lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2)

## the standard error, from xbar to xbar + se
y_s <- dnorm(xbar + se, xbar, se)
arrows(xbar, y_s, xbar + se, y_s, code = 3, length = 0.07, angle = 25,
       col = crukdark, lwd = 1.6)
sl <- "SE = 2.52"; sy <- y_s + strheight(sl, cex = 0.86) * 1.9
rect(xbar + se/2 - strwidth(sl, cex = 0.86) * 0.58, sy - strheight(sl, cex = 0.86) * 1.1,
     xbar + se/2 + strwidth(sl, cex = 0.86) * 0.58, sy + strheight(sl, cex = 0.86) * 1.1,
     col = "white", border = NA)
text(xbar + se / 2, sy, sl, col = crukdark, cex = 0.86, font = 2)

axis(1, at = round(seq(xbar - 3 * se, xbar + 3 * se, 2 * se)),
     cex.axis = 1.0, lwd = 1.1)
mtext("Sample mean (mmHg)", side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 0.92)

## the 95% confidence interval, drawn on the axis
segments(lo, -ymax * 0.055, hi, -ymax * 0.055, col = crukpink, lwd = 2.6, xpd = NA)
segments(c(lo, hi), -ymax * 0.095, c(lo, hi), -ymax * 0.015,
         col = crukpink, lwd = 2.2, xpd = NA)

## the estimate, sitting on the axis
lab <- expression(bolditalic(bar(x)) * bold(" = 133.17"))
ly  <- ymax * 0.30
lw  <- strwidth(lab, cex = 0.98) * 1.08
lh  <- strheight(lab, cex = 0.98) * 1.5
rect(xbar - lw/2, ly - lh, xbar + lw/2, ly + lh, col = "white", border = NA)
text(xbar, ly, lab, col = cruklight, cex = 0.98)
segments(xbar, 0, xbar, ly - lh, col = cruklight, lwd = 1.2)
points(xbar, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.7)

## pink "95% confidence interval" box
lab  <- "95% confidence interval"
lcex <- 0.90
bx <- xbar; by <- ymax * 1.14
bw <- strwidth(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.12
bh <- strheight(lab, cex = lcex) * 1.6
rect(bx - bw/2, by - bh, bx + bw/2, by + bh,
     border = crukpink, lwd = 1.4, col = "white")
text(bx, by, lab, col = crukpink, cex = lcex, font = 2)
for (sgn in c(-1, 1))
  arrows(bx + sgn * bw/2 * 0.8, by - bh, bx + sgn * tcrit * se * 0.96, 0.010,
         length = 0.05, lwd = 1.2, col = crukpink)

text(xbar, ymax * 1.40, "Sampling distribution of the sample mean",
     col = crukdark, cex = 0.92)
dev.off()
```

```{r loss-function, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

pdf("intro-figures/loss-function.pdf", width = 4.6, height = 2.5)
par(mar = c(3.0, 0.6, 0.6, 0.6), mgp = c(1.5, 0.45, 0))

theta <- 0
tobs  <- 1.3
xlim  <- c(-2.4, 2.4)

xs <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 600)

plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, 8.6), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")

## absolute error loss
lines(xs, 2 * abs(xs - theta), col = cruklight, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
## squared error loss
lines(xs, (xs - theta)^2, col = crukdark, lwd = 2.4)

axis(1, at = seq(-2, 2, 1), labels = FALSE, lwd = 1.1)
mtext(expression(hat(theta)), side = 1, line = 1.5, cex = 1.1)

## the estimand
segments(theta, 0, theta, 5.9, col = crukpink, lty = 2, lwd = 1.4)
text(theta, 5.9, expression(theta), pos = 3, offset = 0.05, col = crukpink,
     cex = 1.25, xpd = NA)

## the loss actually incurred by the estimate
segments(tobs, 0, tobs, (tobs - theta)^2, col = crukdark, lwd = 1.2, lty = 3)
points(tobs, (tobs - theta)^2, pch = 19, col = crukdark, cex = 1.3)
points(tobs, 0, pch = 19, col = cruklight, cex = 1.4)
text(tobs + 0.10, (tobs - theta)^2, expression(L(theta, hat(theta))),
     col = crukdark, cex = 0.92, adj = c(0, 0.2))

legend("topleft", bty = "n", cex = 0.86, seg.len = 1.8,
       legend = c(expression((hat(theta) - theta)^2 ~ " squared error"),
                  expression(2 * group("|", hat(theta) - theta, "|") ~ " absolute error")),
       col = c(crukdark, cruklight), lwd = c(2.4, 2), lty = c(1, 2))
dev.off()
```

```{r discrete-parameters, include=FALSE}
crukdark <- "#00007E"; cruklight <- "#009CEE"; crukpink <- "#FF0087"
dfig <- function(file, x, y, ylim, xlab, main, extra = NULL) {
  pdf(file, width = 3.6, height = 2.7)
  par(mar = c(3.1, 4.4, 1.5, 0.5), mgp = c(1.9, 0.5, 0), tcl = -0.3, las = 1, bty = "l",
      cex.axis = 0.95, cex.lab = 1.05, cex.main = 1.1, font.main = 1)
  plot(x, y, type = "h", lwd = 4, lend = 1, col = cruklight, ylim = ylim,
       xlab = xlab, ylab = "", main = main)
  title(ylab = "Probability", line = 3.2)
  if (!is.null(extra)) extra()
  dev.off()
}
## binomial: n = 20 trials, p = 0.4
bx <- 0:20; by <- dbinom(bx, 20, 0.4)
b_n  <- function() { arrows(0, 0.205, 20, 0.205, code = 3, length = 0.06, angle = 25, lwd = 1.4, col = crukdark)
                     text(10, 0.205, "n = 20", pos = 3, offset = 0.25, col = crukdark, cex = 0.95) }
b_np <- function() { segments(8, 0, 8, 0.185, lty = 2, lwd = 1.4, col = crukpink)
                     text(8.4, 0.17, "np = 8", pos = 4, col = crukpink, cex = 0.95) }
dfig("intro-figures/binom-plain.pdf", bx, by, c(0, 0.24), "Number of successes", "Binomial distribution")
dfig("intro-figures/binom-n.pdf",     bx, by, c(0, 0.24), "Number of successes", "Binomial distribution", b_n)
dfig("intro-figures/binom-np.pdf",    bx, by, c(0, 0.24), "Number of successes", "Binomial distribution",
     function() { b_n(); b_np() })
## Poisson: lambda = 4
px <- 0:12; py <- dpois(px, 4)
p_l <- function() { segments(4, 0, 4, 0.215, lty = 2, lwd = 1.4, col = crukpink)
                    text(4.3, 0.205, expression(lambda == 4), pos = 4, col = crukpink, cex = 0.95) }
dfig("intro-figures/pois-plain.pdf", px, py, c(0, 0.23), "Number of events", "Poisson distribution")
dfig("intro-figures/pois-lambda.pdf", px, py, c(0, 0.23), "Number of events", "Poisson distribution", p_l)
```

\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base, xshift=14pt] at (sam.south |- 0,-5.35) {Median $\tilde{x}$ of the sample};
\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base] at (inf.center |- 0,-5.35) {$\longrightarrow$};
\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base, xshift=14pt] at (pop.south |- 0,-5.35) {Median $m$ of the population};
\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base, xshift=14pt] at (sam.south |- 0,-5.95) {Variance $s^2$ of the sample};
\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base] at (inf.center |- 0,-5.95) {$\longrightarrow$};
\node[font=\normalsize, anchor=base, xshift=14pt] at (pop.south |- 0,-5.95) {Variance $\sigma^2$ of the population};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}

```{r pnr-examples, include=FALSE}
crukdark  <- "#00007E"
cruklight <- "#009CEE"
crukpink  <- "#FF0087"

one <- function(file, expr) {
  pdf(file, width = 3.2, height = 2.4)
  par(mar = c(2.2, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4), mgp = c(1.3, 0.4, 0))
  expr
  dev.off()
}

## 1. parametric: a normal distribution, fully described by mu and sigma
one("intro-figures/pnr-parametric.pdf", {
  xs <- seq(-3.6, 3.6, length.out = 800); ys <- dnorm(xs)
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(xs), ylim = c(0, 0.52), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(ys, rep(0, length(xs))), col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2.2)
  segments(0, 0, 0, dnorm(0), col = crukpink, lty = 2, lwd = 1.6)
  text(0, dnorm(0), expression(mu), pos = 3, offset = 0.2, col = crukpink, cex = 1.4)
  y_s <- dnorm(1)
  arrows(0, y_s, 1, y_s, code = 3, length = 0.06, angle = 25, col = crukdark, lwd = 1.5)
  text(0.5, y_s, expression(sigma), pos = 3, offset = 0.2, col = crukdark, cex = 1.3)
  axis(1, at = -3:3, labels = FALSE, lwd = 1)
})

## 2. nonparametric: any distribution that is symmetric about its median
one("intro-figures/pnr-nonparametric.pdf", {
  f <- function(x) 0.5 * dnorm(x, -1.25, 0.65) + 0.5 * dnorm(x, 1.25, 0.65)
  xs <- seq(-3.6, 3.6, length.out = 800); ys <- f(xs)
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(xs), ylim = c(0, 0.52 * max(ys) / 0.40), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(ys, rep(0, length(xs))), col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2.2)
  segments(0, 0, 0, max(ys) * 1.05, col = crukpink, lty = 2, lwd = 1.6)
  text(0, max(ys) * 1.05, expression(italic(m)), pos = 3, offset = 0.2, col = crukpink, cex = 1.4)
  arrows(-0.15, max(ys) * 0.55, -2.4, max(ys) * 0.55, length = 0.06, angle = 25, col = crukdark, lwd = 1.3)
  arrows( 0.15, max(ys) * 0.55,  2.4, max(ys) * 0.55, length = 0.06, angle = 25, col = crukdark, lwd = 1.3)
  text(-1.25, max(ys) * 0.55, "50%", pos = 1, offset = 0.3, col = crukdark, cex = 0.95, font = 2)
  text( 1.25, max(ys) * 0.55, "50%", pos = 1, offset = 0.3, col = crukdark, cex = 0.95, font = 2)
  axis(1, at = -3:3, labels = FALSE, lwd = 1)
})

## 3. robust: a normal distribution contaminated by a few outliers
one("intro-figures/pnr-robust.pdf", {
  set.seed(7)
  x  <- c(qnorm(ppoints(20)), 5.4, 6.1, 6.9)
  xs <- seq(-3.4, 7.6, length.out = 800); ys <- dnorm(xs)
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(xs), ylim = c(-0.07, 0.52), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(ys, rep(0, length(xs))), col = adjustcolor(cruklight, 0.25), border = NA)
  lines(xs, ys, col = crukdark, lwd = 2.2)
  points(x[1:20], rep(-0.035, 20), pch = 19, cex = 0.7, col = crukdark)
  points(x[21:23], rep(-0.035, 3), pch = 19, cex = 1.1, col = crukpink)
  text(6.15, 0.06, "outliers", col = crukpink, cex = 0.95, font = 2)
  segments(median(x), 0, median(x), 0.45, col = cruklight, lwd = 2)
  segments(mean(x),   0, mean(x),   0.37, col = crukpink,  lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  text(median(x) - 0.15, 0.45, "median", col = cruklight, cex = 0.9, font = 2, adj = c(1, 0))
  text(mean(x) + 0.15, 0.33, "mean", col = crukpink, cex = 0.9, font = 2, adj = c(0, 0))
  axis(1, at = seq(-3, 7, 1), labels = FALSE, lwd = 1, pos = -0.07)
})
```

## Central limit theorem (CLT)

\begin{center}
\includegraphics[height=0.54\textheight]{intro-figures/clt-sim.pdf}

\vspace{0.6em}

\textbf{The usefulness of the CLT is that the distribution of sample means\\ approaches normality regardless of the distribution of the population}\\ (provided the observations are independent and identically distributed,\\ with finite variance)
\end{center}

## Estimating parameters: confidence intervals {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em+3.8pt\relax}

\begin{columns}[T]
\begin{column}{0.62\textwidth}
\small\leftskip=1.4pt
\bitem{In frequentist statistics, a confidence interval (CI) gives \textbf{lower and upper bounds} that are likely to contain (in repeated sampling) the true value of an unknown parameter $\theta$}
\vspace{1.2em}
\bitem{It is computed at a pre-defined \textbf{confidence level} (e.g.\ 95\%), which reflects the \textbf{long-run performance of the method}: in repeated sampling, 95\% of the intervals contain $\theta$}
\vspace{1.2em}
\bitem{A 95\% CI does \textbf{not} mean a 95\% probability that $\theta$ lies in \textbf{this particular} interval}
\end{column}
\begin{column}{0.36\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{intro-figures/ci-sim.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

\reference{\url{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidence_interval}, accessed 18 November 2026}

## Confidence interval for $\mu$: $\sigma$ known {.t}

\vspace{0.1em}

\begin{tikzpicture}[
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=3mm]}, line width=1.3pt, draw=crukpink},
  lbl/.style={font=\footnotesize\bfseries, text=crukdark},

              execute at begin node={\hyphenpenalty=10000\raggedright}}]
\useasboundingbox (0,0.1) rectangle (11.4,-7.15);
\begin{scope}[shift={(0.3,-1.45)}]
\fill[cruklight!25] plot[domain=0:2.9, samples=80] (\x,{1.15*exp(-((\x-1.45)^2)/(2*0.45^2))}) -- (2.9,0) -- (0,0) -- cycle;
\draw[cruklight, line width=1.2pt] plot[domain=0:2.9, samples=80] (\x,{1.15*exp(-((\x-1.45)^2)/(2*0.45^2))});
\draw[->, gray] (-0.1,0) -- (3.1,0);
\draw[dashed, crukdark] (1.45,0) -- (1.45,1.25) node[above, inner sep=1pt, font=\footnotesize] {$\mu$};
\node[font=\footnotesize, text=crukdark] at (2.75,1.0) {$N(\mu,\sigma^2)$};
\end{scope}
\node[lbl, anchor=north] at (1.75,-1.5) {Statistical model};
\node[txt] at (3.9,0.134) {\textbf{Assumptions:}\\[2pt] 1.\ the data are continuous\\ 2.\ the data are a random sample from the population\\ 3.\ independent observations $x_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$\\ 4.\ the population is normal, with \textbf{known} $\sigma$};

## Confidence interval for $\mu$: $\sigma$ known {.t}

\vspace{0.1em}

\begin{tikzpicture}[
  arr/.style={-{Stealth[length=3mm]}, line width=1.3pt, draw=crukpink},
  lbl/.style={font=\footnotesize\bfseries, text=crukdark},
  txt/.style={font=\small, text width=7.4cm, align=left, anchor=north west, inner sep=0pt,
              execute at begin node={\hyphenpenalty=10000\raggedright}}]
\useasboundingbox (0,0.1) rectangle (11.4,-7.15);
\begin{scope}[shift={(0.3,-1.45)}]
\fill[cruklight!25] plot[domain=0:2.9, samples=80] (\x,{1.15*exp(-((\x-1.45)^2)/(2*0.45^2))}) -- (2.9,0) -- (0,0) -- cycle;
\draw[cruklight, line width=1.2pt] plot[domain=0:2.9, samples=80] (\x,{1.15*exp(-((\x-1.45)^2)/(2*0.45^2))});
\draw[->, gray] (-0.1,0) -- (3.1,0);
\draw[dashed, crukpink, line width=0.9pt] (1.45,0) -- (1.45,1.25) node[above, inner sep=1pt, font=\footnotesize\bfseries, text=crukpink] {$\mu = {?}$};
\node[font=\footnotesize, text=crukdark] at (2.75,1.0) {$N(\mu,\sigma^2)$};
\end{scope}
\node[lbl, anchor=north] at (1.75,-1.5) {Statistical model};
\node[txt] at (3.9,0.134) {\textbf{Assumptions:}\\[2pt] 1.\ the data are continuous\\ 2.\ the data are a random sample from the population\\ 3.\ independent observations $x_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$\\ 4.\ the population is normal, with \textbf{known} $\sigma$};

\node[txt] at (3.9,0.134) {\textbf{Assumptions:}\\[2pt] 1.\ the data are continuous\\ 2.\ the data are a random sample from the population\\ 3.\ independent observations $x_i$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$\\ 4.\ the population is normally distributed};
\node[txt] at (3.9,-2.45) {\textbf{Hypotheses:}\\[2pt] $H_0$: $\mu = \mu_0$ \qquad $H_1$: $\mu \neq \mu_0$};

## Wilcoxon signed-rank test {.t}

\vspace{-0.2em}

\bitem{Tests whether the \textbf{median} equals a hypothesised value $m_0$; the nonparametric counterpart of the one-sample $t$-test}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bitem{Works on the \textbf{ranks} of the differences from $m_0$ instead of the raw values}

\vspace{0.8em}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Assumptions}}

\vspace{0.2em}

\sitem{observations are independent}
\sitem{differences from $m_0$ can be meaningfully ranked}
\sitem{the distribution is \textbf{symmetric} around its median}

\vspace{0.8em}

\textbf{\textcolor{crukdark}{Hypotheses}}

\vspace{0.2em}

\sitem{$H_0$: median $= m_0$}
\sitem{$H_1$: median $\neq m_0$ (two-sided), or $>m_0$ / $<m_0$ (one-sided)}

## Wilcoxon signed-rank test: step by step {.t}

\vspace{-0.2em}

\bitem{\circnum{1} \textbf{Differences:} $d_i = x_i - m_0$ for every observation}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bitem{\circnum{2} \textbf{Drop the zeros} ($x_i = m_0$): they carry no information, so $n$ is the number of non-zero differences}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bitem{\circnum{3} \textbf{Rank the absolute differences} $|d_i|$ from smallest (rank 1) to largest (rank $n$); ties get the average rank}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bitem{\circnum{4} \textbf{Attach the signs:} each rank keeps the sign of its difference}

\vspace{0.5em}

\bitem{\circnum{5} \textbf{Test statistic:} $W^{+}$ = sum of ranks of the positive differences, $W^{-}$ = sum of ranks of the negative ones}

\sitem{check: $W^{+} + W^{-} = n(n+1)/2$}

## Wilcoxon signed-rank test: worked example {.t}

\vspace{-0.2em}

Tumour sizes (mm) of 8 patients, $H_0$: median $= 10$

\vspace{0.4em}

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\columncolor{cruklight!20}}c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Patient} & $\boldsymbol{x}$ & $\boldsymbol{d = x-10}$ & $\boldsymbol{|d|}$ & \textbf{Rank} & \textbf{Sign} \\ \hline
1 & 12.1 & 2.1 & 2.1 & 4 & $+$ \\ \hline
2 & 9.5 & $-0.5$ & 0.5 & 1 & $-$ \\ \hline
3 & 14.0 & 4.0 & 4.0 & 6 & $+$ \\ \hline
4 & 10.0 & 0 & & dropped & \\ \hline
5 & 11.3 & 1.3 & 1.3 & 3 & $+$ \\ \hline
6 & 8.2 & $-1.8$ & 1.8 & 2 & $-$ \\ \hline
7 & 15.5 & 5.5 & 5.5 & 7 & $+$ \\ \hline
8 & 13.0 & 3.0 & 3.0 & 5 & $+$ \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.3em}

$n = 7$, \quad $W^{+} = 4+6+3+7+5 = \textbf{25}$, \quad $W^{-} = 1+2 = 3$, \quad $25+3 = 28 = \frac{7\cdot 8}{2}$

## Wilcoxon signed-rank test: step by step {.t}

\vspace{-0.2em}

\bitem{\circnum{6} \textbf{Null distribution:} under $H_0$ every rank is equally likely to carry a $+$ or $-$ sign, so $W^{+}$ has a known discrete distribution}

\sitem{mean $= n(n+1)/4$, \quad variance $= n(n+1)(2n+1)/24$}
\sitem{small $n$ ($\lesssim 25$, no ties): use the \textbf{exact} distribution}
\sitem{larger $n$: normal approximation, $z = \dfrac{W^{+} - n(n+1)/4}{\sqrt{n(n+1)(2n+1)/24}}$, with continuity and tie corrections}

\vspace{0.3em}

\bitem{\circnum{7} \textbf{$p$-value:} probability of a $W^{+}$ at least as extreme as observed under $H_0$}

\sitem{example: $W^{+} = 25$ against an expected 14, so $p \approx 0.047$ (two-sided)}

\vspace{0.3em}

\bitem{\circnum{8} \textbf{Decision:} reject $H_0$ if $p < \alpha$ (typically 0.05)}

\vspace{0.3em}

\keybox{\small Median tumour size differs from 10 mm ($\boldsymbol{p \approx 0.047}$)}


## Parametric tests vs non-parametric tests {.t}

\vspace{-0.3em}

\small\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\columncolor{cruklight!20}}p{2.3cm}|p{4.1cm}|p{4.1cm}|}
\hline
 & \textbf{Parametric} & \textbf{Non-parametric} \\ \hline
\textbf{Assumption} & Specific distribution (e.g.\ normal, equal variances) & Little or none (often just symmetry or similar shape) \\ \hline
\textbf{Tests about} & Parameters (mean, variance) & Medians, distributions, ranks \\ \hline
\textbf{Uses} & Actual data values & Ranks or signs \\ \hline
\textbf{Power} & Higher when assumptions hold & Lower if the data really are normal, though often only slightly \\ \hline
\textbf{Robustness} & Sensitive to outliers and skew & More robust \\ \hline
\textbf{Data types} & Quantitative (interval/ratio) & Quantitative, ordinal and sometimes nominal \\ \hline
\textbf{Small samples} & Hard to check assumptions & Often the safer choice \\ \hline
\end{tabular}

## Unequal variance $t$-test (i.e.\ Welch's $t$-test) {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em-1.9pt\relax}

\textbf{Distribution of the test statistic under $\boldsymbol{H_0}$:}\par
approximately a $t$-distribution with $\nu$ degrees of freedom (Welch--Satterthwaite):

\[\nu \approx \frac{\left(s_1^2/n_1 + s_2^2/n_2\right)^2}{\dfrac{(s_1^2/n_1)^2}{n_1 - 1} + \dfrac{(s_2^2/n_2)^2}{n_2 - 1}}\]

\begin{center}
\includegraphics[height=0.42\textheight]{intro-figures/tdist.pdf}
\end{center}

## Wilcoxon rank-sum test: step by step {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em-1.9pt\relax}

\textbf{Distribution of the test statistic under $\boldsymbol{H_0}$:}

\vspace{0.4em}

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.3}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\columncolor{cruklight!20}}l|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
$\boldsymbol{W}$ & 6 & 7 & 8 & 9 & 10 & 11 & 12 \\ \hline
\textbf{Probability} & 1/10 & 1/10 & 2/10 & 2/10 & 2/10 & 1/10 & 1/10 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\vspace{0.6em}

\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{\hspace{1.5em}}l@{}}
One-sided $p$-value: & $P(W \geq 12) = 1/10 = 0.1$ \\
Two-sided $p$-value: & $\min(1,\ 2 \times 1/10) = 0.2$ \\
\end{tabular}

\vspace{1em}

\keybox{At the significance level $\boldsymbol{\alpha = 0.05}$, we cannot reject the null hypothesis ($\boldsymbol{G = F}$)}

\vspace{0.6em}

```{=latex}
{\small\setbox0\hbox{\textit{Note:}}\hangindent=\dimexpr\wd0+\fontdimen2\font\relax\hangafter=1\noindent\textit{Note:} with $n_1 = 3$ and $n_2 = 2$ the smallest possible two-sided $p$-value is $2/10 = 0.2$, so $H_0$ can never be rejected at $\alpha = 0.05$\par}
```

## \fontsize{16.2}{18}\selectfont Parametric, non-parametric and distribution-free tests {.t}

\vspace{\dimexpr-0.2em+0.8pt\relax}

\small

\bitem{\textcolor{crukdark}{\textbf{Non-parametric}} test: the hypothesis is \textbf{not} about a parameter of the population}

\vspace{0.3em}

\bitem{\textcolor{crukdark}{\textbf{Distribution-free}} test: it makes \textbf{no assumptions} about the precise form of the sampled population, or its assumptions are never so elaborate as to imply a population whose distribution is \textbf{completely specified}}

\vspace{0.8em}

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|}
\hline
\rowcolor{cruklight!20}\textbf{Non-parametric, distribution-free tests} & \textbf{Parametric, distribution-dependent tests} \\ \hline
Wilcoxon rank-sum test & Two-sample Student's $t$-test \\
 & Unequal variance $t$-test (i.e.\ Welch's $t$-test) \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\reference{Bradley, J.\,V. \textit{Distribution-Free Statistical Tests}. Englewood Cliffs, NJ: Prentice-Hall (1968)\\ Kendall, M.\,G. \& Sundrum, R.\,M. \textit{Distribution-free methods and order properties}. Rev.\ Int.\ Stat.\ Inst.\ \textbf{21}(3), 124--134 (1953)}
